title: Sacred Band of Thebes
capsule: The Sacred Band (Ἱερὸς Λόχος) was an elite Theban military unit of 300 men — traditionally 150 pairs of male lovers — formed around 379 BCE under the general Gorgidas and reorganized by Pelopidas, who deployed it as a concentrated shock force rather than dispersed among the ranks. The Band formed the spearhead of Theban victories at Leuctra (371 BCE), where it helped Epaminondas break the Spartan right wing with the oblique assault, and at Mantinea (362 BCE). It met its end at the Battle of Chaeronea in 338 BCE when Philip II of Macedon's forces, with the young Alexander commanding the left wing, annihilated the unit; Philip reportedly wept when he saw their bodies lying in formation, unwilling to retreat.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Sacred Band's existence, composition, and fate at Chaeronea are well documented in Plutarch and Diodorus Siculus; its precise territorial role as a polity-level entity is unconventional and the Wikidata from/to dates reflect the period of Theban military hegemony rather than a territorial state.
